name: AC Milan 2006/07 (Carlo Ancelotti)
scopeNote: AC Milan from the Champions League third qualifying round (2006-08-09) to the last Serie A match (2007-05-27), including the 2007-05-23 final win over Liverpool in Athens. Style named by sources: 4-3-2-1 'Christmas tree' (albero di Natale) with Pirlo regista, Gattuso and Ambrosini as mezzalas, Seedorf and Kaka behind a lone striker (Gilardino, Inzaghi). Evidence is concentrated on the Champions League knockout rounds (Celtic, Bayern, Manchester United, Liverpool); Serie A (Milan started with a Calciopoli points deduction) is thinly covered. Coaches' Voice 4-3-2-1 explainer is a general piece naming Ancelotti's Milan without a season, kept retrospectiveOnly. 2005 (Istanbul, diamond/4-4-1-1) and 2007/08 material was excluded. Several event dates are month-level because the source gives only the round. The sempremilan 2021 Milan v Man Utd piece (Pioli) was read and excluded as out of period.
openQuestions: Seedorf's line: Coaches' Voice and Sempremilan place Seedorf and Kaka as the two behind the striker, while the Sempremilan analysis also has Seedorf dropping to share the defensive-midfield role with Gattuso. Confirm whether this was a recurring pattern or one match (Man Utd 3-0).

Whether Milan zone-marked or man-marked: Sempremilan says forwards and midfielders man-marked United's defenders when pressing and Ronaldo was doubled by Oddo and Gattuso/Ambrosini, yet also says midfielders worked on zonal principles. No tier A source on Milan's 2006/07 marking found.

The final's tactical shape against Liverpool is described only through lineups and goals; no tier A-B analysis of Athens (pressing, line height) was found. Spielverlagerung and Coaches' Voice pieces on the 2007 final were not located.
Pre-season origin of the Christmas tree (2002 Trofeo Berlusconi per Gulf Times) is outside the period; the 2006/07 shape was adjusted after Shevchenko left, but no source dated to 2006 was found.
The 2026-dated Ancelotti quotes (RSI 2025, Instagram 2020) are retrospective; the original 2006/07 press quotes were not found.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: Ancelotti brought in a 4-3-2-1 system, famously nicknamed the Christmas tree because of its tree-like shape. He opted for a back four while having a midfield three and two inside forwards with a lone striker up front.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: Kaka’s role: The Brazilian was the star of the team. He was a player with explosive dribbling along with ability to find pockets of space between the line he was given the license to roam by Ancelotti.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: To a casual observer Andrea Pirlo was a defensive, but for those familiar he was a Regista, a playmaker who sat in front of the defence and created attacks from deep.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: Pirlo, with his unique passing ability, could angle balls into onrushing full-backs who could bomb forward and cross the ball.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: Gattuso and Ambrosini were the mezzala’s or the half-wingers. They were the engine of the side: they ran around, defended the central areas, prevented counters, helped in building up play and protected Pirlo to allow him to play his natural game.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: Being a disciple of none other than Arrigo Sacchi himself, Ancelotti had granted freedom to these four midfield players who operated along the lines of zonal principles rather than a fixed position.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: Another positional switch was seen when Seedorf sat back with Gattuso as a defensive midfielder to allow Ambrosini and Pirlo to advance and join the attack. This way Milan had a way to protect against counter-attacks but had players committed in United’s box.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: Whenever Milan needed to slowly build their attacks, one of the midfielders would drop in between the centre-backs and collect the ball.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: He was also always available as a passing options to his team for counter-attacks once they won the ball back.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: Pressing from Milan: Of course this was 2007 and pressing wasn’t as intense as how Klopp or Pep Guardiola uses it now, but Ancelotti had his forwards and midfielders man mark whenever United’s defenders had the ball.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: Milan’s second goal came as a result of clever pressing from Inzaghi and Pirlo. Vidic was pressed by Inzaghi and Pirlo pressed Heinze.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: Whenever United’s players had the ball towards the touchline, Milan would commit more players towards the sides and try and reduce the playing area.

sources.title: Ancelotti outsmarts Sir Alex: Tactical analysis of 'La Partita Perfetta' against Man Utd
sources.evidence: With a lean frame he wasn’t the best at holding up the ball, but he helped with pressing and occupied defenders and pulled them away to create space for Kaka. He also acted as the target man for all crosses inside the box.

sources.title: The pioneering AC Milan Lab that extended players' careers
sources.evidence: In fact, this team was the oldest, wisest group of players to walk out for a Champions League final in the tournament’s history. Just four of those in the starting line-up were below the age of 30, and three of them were in their late-20s. Only Kaká provided some semblance of youth at 25.

sources.title: The pioneering AC Milan Lab that extended players' careers
sources.evidence: They ran out 2-1 winners thanks to a double from Filippo Inzaghi, their 33-year-old poacher. Their captain, the resolute Paolo Maldini, became the oldest to lift the trophy at 37.

sources.title: The pioneering AC Milan Lab that extended players' careers
sources.evidence: The Milan Lab worked so well for its incumbent beneficiaries that the club began to sign older players, safe in the knowledge that their careers could be prolonged too.

sources.title: The pioneering AC Milan Lab that extended players' careers
sources.evidence: Within a year, the Milan Lab was proving its worth. The number of total practice days lost had decreased, as had the club’s use of medicine. Injuries had lowered drastically.

sources.title: The 4-3-2-1 formation: football tactics explained - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Carlo Ancelotti — who won the 2003 and 2007 Champions Leagues as Milan head coach — utilised a 4-3-2-1 shape during his spell at the San Siro. He based it around the influence of Andrea Pirlo as a central pivot in the midfield trio.

sources.title: The 4-3-2-1 formation: football tactics explained - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: Pirlo was flanked by Gennaro Gattuso and Massimo Ambrosini, both of whom could press, duel and defend the central spaces when in a block, or jumping out to press.

sources.title: The 4-3-2-1 formation: football tactics explained - Coaches' Voice
sources.evidence: The 4-3-2-1 lacks natural width in attack, not least immediate width when regaining possession, ready for an attacking transition. It can be easy for the opposition to gain ground and progress through the wide areas, in defensive transition.
